callPoints: **Guidance cut:** FY27 revenue growth 1.5-3.0% in constant currency (was 1.5-3.5% in April), now including ~1.7% from the Optimum Healthcare IT and Stratus acquisitions. Like-for-like, organic growth at the midpoint fell from ~2.2% to ~0.5-0.8%. Operating margin guidance kept at 20-22%.

**Why:** a ~50 bp one-off from an EURS client terminating a programme late in the quarter, volumes weaker than plan and than normal Q1 seasonality, and less price increase than planned because clients ask for AI productivity and competition is intense. A large European manufacturing client now costs >1% of growth (0.75-1% assumed in April), partly because Infosys chose not to bid on deals 'that did not make economic sense'; that deal ends in December.

**AI-led deflation acknowledged:** 'On the back of AI, there is an additional deflation or the AI-led deflation... not only on the large deal portion, that is also there on the non-large deal portion' (CFO). Infosys tracks it but does not quantify it. Clients also ask for productivity in mid-contract, not only at renewal (CEO).

**AI revenue:** 'AI-first' services (six areas of the 'Hexagon' strategy: AI strategy & engineering, data, process, legacy modernisation, physical AI, trust) were 8.2% of revenue, up from 5.5% in Q3FY26 and growing double digits a quarter; management says it is not a reclassification. 80,000+ delivery staff use coding tools such as Claude Code and Codex; plan for 6,000 'frontier engineers'.

**Deals:** 22 large deals worth US$3.6 bn, 61% net new; three of ~US$400 mn each; 20% of TCV from vendor-consolidation wins (US$700 mn net new from six such deals, at 'very healthy margins'). Deal tenure unchanged at 3-5 years.

**Costs and people:** wage hikes for most staff from October 2026 and for senior staff from January 2027; 20,000 graduate hires planned for FY27 (4,000 in Q1); no restructuring - reskilling instead. Utilisation excl. trainees 84.9%. Onsite mix to fall another 0.75-1% (excl. acquisitions) this year.

**CEO succession:** the board named Ashiss Dash (31 years at Infosys, head of the EURS vertical) CEO-designate; he takes over on 1-Apr-2027 when Salil Parekh's term ends. Infosys decided not to invest in data centres.
**Tax and cash:** FY27 effective tax rate 29-30%; yield on cash 6.8%; cash US$3.9 bn after paying >US$1 bn of dividends in the quarter.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Infosys (consolidated, Rs crore). Infosys is modelled in US dollars first: US$ revenue by vertical (the eight business segments the company discloses) in `usdBuild`, converted at a stated Rs/US$ path; the engine then runs on the resulting rupee revenue growth (`revenueGrowth`) and an EBITDA margin. EBITDA = Screener operating profit before other income and depreciation; the company's EBIT (operating) margin = EBITDA margin less depreciation & amortisation, which we show next to it. The authoring script checks that the US$ build times the Rs/US$ rate equals model revenue. Net profit is attributable to shareholders (tools/authoring/INFY.patch.js); the tax line also carries minorities. Other income = treasury yield on opening net cash + non-treasury items, built from the AR FY26 other-income note (2.19). Valued on P/E, as the street does.

usdBuild._why: US$ revenue by vertical. FY26 base = sum of the four quarters (US$ revenue x reported mix, fact sheets); total FY26 US$20,158 mn. FY27 guidance (23-Jul-2026): 1.5-3.0% constant currency, including ~1.7% from the Optimum Healthcare IT and Stratus acquisitions, >1% drag from a large European manufacturing client and 0.75-1% from moving work offshore; FS and EURS to grow above the company average, Retail and Communication weak. Q1FY27: +2.4% YoY cc, +1.0% QoQ (0.5% lost to an EURS programme termination). Growth rates are US$ (we assume no net cross-currency effect after Q1).

growthWhy.fs: FY27 +3.1%: grew 5.4% in FY26 and 2.8% (2.4% cc) in Q1FY27; ~US$1 bn of net new large-deal TCV in Q1 and Stratus (insurance, closed Apr-2026, ~0.25% of company revenue) inside it; management expects FS above the company average. FY28-29 +4.5%: large-deal ramp-ups, vendor consolidation, offset by AI-led price deflation on renewals.
growthWhy.mfg: FY27 -2%: lower revenue from one large European manufacturing client (>1% of company revenue; part of it a deal Infosys chose not to pursue, ending in December) and a weak European auto market; Q1 +1.5% YoY. FY28 +1% (the client is fully out of the base only from Q4FY27), FY29 +3%.
growthWhy.eurs: FY27 +2.5%: a client terminated a programme in Q1 (~0.5% of company revenue, one-off); management still expects EURS above average (80% of FY26 large-deal TCV was net new, utilities demand from grids and data centres). FY28-29 +4-4.5%.
growthWhy.retail: FY27 -1%: consumer budgets 'tightly controlled', clients asking for AI productivity commitments (Q1 -1.8% YoY). Slow recovery after.
growthWhy.comm: FY27 -0.5%: Q1 +2.9% YoY but management calls the vertical challenged and budgets flat to negative; FY26 growth came from large-deal ramp-ups that have now annualised. FY28 +2%, FY29 +2.5%.
growthWhy.hitech: FY27 flat: Q1 +1.6% YoY; tech clients are the earliest adopters of AI coding tools, which compresses classic work.
growthWhy.ls: FY27 +22%: Optimum Healthcare IT (agreement Mar-2026 for up to US$465 mn incl. earn-outs; closed in Q1FY27; ~1.5% of company revenue a year at a ~1.7% combined acquisition contribution less Stratus) plus ~2% organic. Q1FY27 life sciences +26.8% YoY. FY28 +6% (small carry-over), FY29 +5%.
growthWhy.others: Shrinking for two years (-12% YoY in Q1FY27); held flat after FY27.

fx._why: Rs/US$ conversion rate. FY26 average 88.6 (Rs178,650 cr / US$20,158 mn); Q1FY27 94.9 (Rs48,211 cr / US$5,082 mn); spot 95.81 at the 30-Sep-2026 close (PTI). FY27 95.5 = Q1 actual, ~95.6 for Q2 and the 30-Sep spot for H2. FY28-29: ~2% depreciation a year, roughly the rupee's forward premium and well below its ~3.7% a year average fall since FY20 on Infosys's own conversion rates (71.0 in FY20). Each 1% of rupee depreciation adds 15-17 bp to the operating margin (CFO, Jul-2026), before any reinvestment.

assumptions._revenueWhy: Rupee revenue = US$ build x Rs/US$. US$ growth +2.0% (FY27E), +3.0% (FY28E), +3.6% (FY29E); rupee growth +9.9% / +5.2% / +5.7%, of which ~7.8 / 2.1 / 2.1 points are the weaker rupee. FY27: Q1 US$5,082 mn; we assume Q2 +1.5% QoQ (full quarter of Optimum), Q3-Q4 roughly flat (furloughs, the European client's deal ending in December), i.e. ~2% cc, close to the 2.25% guidance midpoint and PL's 2.0%. FY28-29: organic growth of 3-3.5% - AI services (8.2% of revenue in Q1FY27, growing double digits a quarter) and large-deal ramp-ups offset 3-3.5% a year of AI-led price deflation on the rest (Kotak's assumption, Jul-2026). No acquisitions after Optimum/Stratus are assumed; Versent (75% for up to A$233 mn, pending regulatory approval) is excluded, as in the company's guidance.
assumptions._marginWhy: Company EBIT (operating) margin: 21.1% (FY25), 21.0% adjusted / 20.3% reported (FY26, Labour Codes charge Rs1,289 cr), 21.1% in Q1FY27; guidance 20-22% kept in Jul-2026. We model EBIT of ~21.0% in each year: rupee depreciation (+70 bp in Q1 alone) and Project Maximus (pricing, utilisation 84.9%, offshore mix, lean automation: +20-30 bp a quarter) offset wage hikes (October 2026 for most staff, January 2027 for seniors), ~50 bp of acquisition costs (amortisation, retention pay) and AI investments; FY28-29 carry AI price deflation against continued offshoring. EBITDA margin (Screener basis) = EBIT + D&A (~2.6% of revenue): FY26 23.7%, Q1FY27 23.7%. Brokers (Jul-2026) model EBIT of 19.8-21.3% for FY27-28.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs2,201 cr (FY24), Rs2,237 cr (FY25), Rs2,727 cr (FY26) = ~1.5% of revenue; we assume Rs2,900 / 3,000 / 3,200 cr. FY27E also includes ~Rs4,400 cr for the Optimum Healthcare IT and Stratus acquisitions (goodwill and intangibles rose US$466 mn in Q1FY27, IFRS balance sheet): an engine workaround, because the model has no acquisition line. Putting the purchase price into FY27 capex takes the cash out of the treasury and lets the acquired intangibles amortise through depreciation. The DCF starts in FY28 and is unaffected.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs4,902 cr = 8.6% of average gross block (Rs57,227 cr; Screener's gross block includes goodwill and right-of-use assets). Q1FY27 Rs1,246 cr (Rs4,984 cr annualised) before a full quarter of the new acquisitions. 8.0% on a gross block lifted by the FY27 acquisitions gives ~Rs5,100 cr in FY27E (2.6% of revenue), ~Rs5,500 cr in FY28E.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to OPENING net cash on Screener's basis (cash Rs22,201 cr + investments Rs21,880 cr - lease liabilities Rs9,176 cr = Rs34,905 cr at Mar-26). The company earned 6.7% on its gross cash and investments in FY26 and 6.8% in Q1FY27 (CFO). 9.0% on opening net cash equals ~6.6-6.9% on the average gross balance in our forecasts, because lease interest is charged separately (interest line) and cash builds through the year; the report shows the implied gross yield for each year. FY26 treasury income (AR note 2.19): interest Rs2,693 cr + gains on funds and bonds Rs393 cr = Rs3,086 cr on average cash and investments of Rs45,312 cr (6.8%).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income, only recurring items (AR FY26 note 2.19): net exchange gains (forward/option losses Rs2,451 cr against translation gains Rs2,948 cr = +Rs497 cr; FY25 +Rs259 cr) and miscellaneous income excluding the Rs165 cr profit on sale of property (Rs153 cr). We hold Rs650 cr. Left out as non-recurring: interest on income-tax refunds (Rs421 cr FY26, Rs343 cr FY25, Rs1,933 cr FY24) and property sale gains. FY27E total other income ~Rs3,790 cr vs Rs3,736 cr underlying in FY26 (Rs4,322 cr less tax-refund interest and the property gain) and Rs3,883 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (Screener Rs2,975 cr plus the Labour Codes charge, less Q4FY26 tax-refund interest): flat, because the Rs18,000 cr buyback (Dec-2025) cut the cash pile by about a third before it rebuilds.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs416 cr; Q1FY27 Rs119 cr (more leases with the acquisitions). No borrowings other than leases (Rs9,176 cr at Mar-26).
assumptions._taxWhy: Guidance: effective tax rate 29-30% for FY27 (Apr and Jul 2026). Q1FY27 29.5% (Rs3,253 cr on Rs11,028 cr). FY26 26.3% reported, flattered by Rs774 cr of reversals of prior-year provisions after favourable tax orders. 29.6% includes minorities (~0.1% of PBT; Rs34 cr in FY26). SEZ tax holidays keep expiring, so we do not assume a lower rate later.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividends only. FY26 DPS Rs48 (interim Rs23 + final Rs25) = 67% of reported EPS of Rs71.58; FY25 Rs43 (67%). Policy (from FY25): return ~85% of free cash flow over five years through dividends and/or buybacks/special dividends and raise the DPS every year; FY25-26 returned Rs55,523 cr = 82.1% of FCF incl. the Rs18,000 cr buyback. The engine cannot reduce the share count, so the buyback part of the policy (~20% of profit a year) stays in the treasury and earns interest; at a P/E of ~12x a buyback would add ~1% more to EPS a year than the interest, which we leave out (conservative).

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, cash-rich, but now exposed to a technology shift that could shrink its core market; 0.9 gives an 11.9% cost of equity, above the 11.3% we use for defensive consumer franchises.
dcf._tgWhy: Rupee terminal growth of 5%: ~3% US$ growth for a mature services company plus ~2% rupee depreciation. Below the 5-6% house range for domestic compounders because AI may shrink the traditional services pool.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Rupee revenue growth fades from ~5.6% (FY29E) to 5.5% over ten years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades from 23.7% to 23.0% (EBIT ~20.4%, the bottom half of today's 20-22% band): AI deflation and pricing pressure erode margins slowly.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~1.5% of revenue, as in FY24-26.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: AI services (8% of revenue, growing double digits a quarter) become large enough to outrun deflation, discretionary spending returns in FY28 and Versent closes: US$ growth ~4% in FY27 and ~5% in FY28-29, EBIT margin ~21.7%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: AI-led deflation accelerates at renewals and clients insource with AI tools: US$ revenue flat to down in FY28-29, pricing cuts push EBIT margin to ~19.8%, the bottom of the guided band.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Infosys: P/E on FY28E EPS (Motilal Oswal and 360 ONE 14x, PL and Choice 15x, ICICI Securities, Nirmal Bang and Nuvama 13x; Jul-2026). 16.5x = Infosys's 23.3x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (forwardMedian; no trough years; 23.8x on EPS before tax-order one-offs) cut by the -29.0% median de-rating of the IT peer set versus each peer's five-year median P/E at the 30-Sep-2026 close (TCS -53%, Wipro -40%, LTIMindtree -38%, LTTS -31%, Mphasis -27%, HCLTech -21%, Persistent -18%, Coforge -11%) = 16.55x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. House rule for all IT reports: full peer set, excluding the company itself and Tech Mahindra (its FY24-25 earnings trough distorts both its current and its median P/E); no sub-sets. No growth or returns adjustment. Sensitivity: on the three large incumbents only (TCS, Wipro, HCLTech; median -40%) the multiple would be 14x. Cross-checks: a justified P/E of 13.7x (90% cash payout, 11.9% cost of equity, 5% growth); 16.5x needs ~6.1% long-run growth. Bull 20x (its 25th-percentile forward P/E since 2021, 19.7x); bear 11x (justified P/E at 4% growth, ~15% below its lowest forward P/E since 2021).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 10x Sep-28E EBITDA = Infosys's 16.6x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, cut by the same -29% IT sector de-rating (11.8x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~15% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (Rs43,745 cr) = 10.2x, rounded. Bull 12x, bear 7x scale with the P/E multiples.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 10-year FCFF, Ke 11.9%, terminal growth 5%, plus net cash.

cover.headline: The growth has gone and may not fully return; the cash, the margins and a 12x multiple make it worth owning anyway
cover.lead: Infosys is India's second-largest IT services company: US$20.2 bn of revenue in FY26, 328,000 people, ~2,000 large clients. The 2026 fall in IT shares is, in our view, mostly a lasting de-rating rather than a cycle: Infosys's volumes were flat in FY26, it now openly talks of "AI-led deflation" in renewals, and in Jul-2026 it cut FY27 guidance to 1.5-3.0% in constant currency even though 1.7 points now come from acquisitions, leaving ~0.5% organic growth. But it still earns a ~21% operating margin, converts more than all its profit into cash and returns ~85% of it. The street values Infosys on **P/E (13-15x FY28E EPS)**. We forecast US$ revenue growth of 2.0% / 3.0% / 3.5% (FY27-29E) and EPS of ₹77.4 / ₹82.0 / ₹88.2, slightly above the street because of the weaker rupee. Applying **16.5x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹85.1** - its own 23.3x median forward P/E cut by the IT sector's median de-rating of −29% - gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with BUY**. Most of the upside is the multiple recovering from ~12x, not earnings growth. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,385, DCF ₹1,347. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Constant-currency growth was 4.2% (FY25), 3.1% (FY26) and 2.4% YoY in Q1FY27; organic revenue fell 0.1% QoQ in Q1. Clients ask for AI productivity at every renewal and now mid-contract; headcount has barely moved (323,578 in Mar-25, 328,062 in Jun-26). We model only ~3-3.5% US$ growth in FY28-29.

arguments.h: Margins and cash are the anchor
arguments.p: EBIT margin ~21% for four years (21.1% in Q1FY27, guidance 20-22%); free cash flow above 100% of profit; no debt; ₹37,065 cr of cash and investments at Jun-26. The 85%-of-FCF payout policy means a ~5% dividend yield at ₹994 plus buybacks.

AI-first services rose from 5.5% to 8.2% of revenue in two quarters and large deals are strong (US$3.6 bn in Q1, 61% net new; 20% from vendor consolidation). But AI also shrinks the work in the other ~92%. Our forecasts assume the two roughly cancel; the bear case assumes they do not.

At ₹994 Infosys trades at 12.1x our FY28E EPS against a 23.3x median forward P/E since 2021 (Infosys −49% vs its five-year median trailing P/E). Our 16.5x applies the IT sector's median de-rating (−29%) to that history; on the large incumbents' deeper de-rating alone it would be 14x, and a justified P/E is 13.7x - so the target needs the market to stop marking Infosys down. On our ten-year cash flows the price implies long-run growth of −2.4% a year.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether organic growth turns positive after Q1's -0.1% QoQ, how much the October wage hikes cost, and whether the 1.5-3.0% guidance holds.
CEO transition: Ashiss Dash is mentored from October 2026 and takes over on 1-Apr-2027; his first FY28 guidance (April 2027) will show whether Infosys resets its strategy or targets.
Capital return: FY25-26 returned 82.1% of free cash flow; another buyback or special dividend would keep the policy on track while cash rebuilds after the Dec-2025 buyback.
AI revenue share each quarter (8.2% in Q1FY27) against the pace of AI-led price deflation in renewals - the single most important number for the multiple.
US policy: H-1B and L-1 fees (from 9-Sep-2026), the DOJ investigation into H-1B classification for one client, tariffs and US interest rates.

blocks.p: Indian IT services grew for three decades on labour arbitrage: an Indian engineer cost a fraction of a Western one, and clients moved application maintenance, testing and infrastructure work offshore. The large incumbents (TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, Wipro, Tech Mahindra) now earn US$6-30 bn each and grow slowly; mid-sized firms (LTIMindtree, Persistent, Coforge, Mphasis) have grown faster by focusing on fewer clients and newer work. Two things changed in 2025-26. Generative AI tools began writing and testing code, so clients expect the same work for less money. And the cycle turned: European industry, retail and telecom clients cut discretionary projects. The table below shows how the forces stood on 30-Sep-2026.

sections.title: Cyclical slowdown or lasting de-rating? Mostly lasting

blocks.p: Indian IT shares fell hard in 2026: the Nifty IT index lost ~14% in seven sessions in February after a new Anthropic AI tool triggered a global sell-off in software and outsourcing stocks, was down ~25% for the year by June and ~24% by early September (Business Today, AIM). Infosys fell from ~₹1,650 at the end of January to ₹994 on 30-Sep-2026 (−41%). Its trailing P/E is 49% below its five-year median; TCS's is 53% below. The question that decides the stock is whether this is a cyclical slowdown that will reverse, or a lasting loss of value because generative AI shrinks the traditional services work these companies sell.

bullets: **What AI does to the business model.** Infosys is paid mostly for effort. If AI tools let 80 people do the work of 100, a client renewing a contract expects to pay less; the CFO calls this "AI-led deflation" and says it now appears mid-contract as well as at renewal. Kotak assumes 3-3.5% a year of deflation for incumbents. Infosys does not quantify it.

**What AI gives back.** New work: building agents, preparing data, modernising legacy code (e.g. 3 mn lines of COBOL for Hertz at 60% lower cost), AI-led operations. This is 8.2% of revenue and growing double digits a quarter. Management compares it to digital (20% to 60% of revenue in a few years) but gives no target; the definition is its own.

**Why the cycle is not the whole story.** Volumes were flat in FY26 even before the 2026 macro shocks, the deflation is described as broad across verticals, and the FY27 cut came despite strong deal wins. Large-deal TCV now converts into less revenue, because renewals are repriced.

**Why it is not a collapse either.** Clients still need someone to run, secure and integrate their systems and to deploy AI inside them; vendor consolidation favours large, trusted suppliers; margins and cash have not cracked; and the industry has absorbed earlier productivity shifts (automation, cloud) by moving to new work.

blocks.callout: **Our verdict:** Mostly lasting. The cyclical parts are real but the business has shifted from volume growth to price-led, near-zero organic growth, and the company itself says AI deflation is now part of every renewal. We do not assume the multiple returns to its 2021-25 range: we apply the IT sector's median de-rating to Infosys's own history. In numbers: we assume organic US$ growth of only ~3-3.5% in FY28-29 (AI work offsetting deflation), a flat ~21% EBIT margin, and a target multiple of 16.5x: Infosys's own median forward P/E cut by the IT peer group's median de-rating (−29%), well below its 2021-25 range. On the large incumbents' deeper de-rating alone (TCS, Wipro, HCLTech; median −40%) it would be 14x: that gap is the main risk to our target.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Infosys has a real but narrow moat. Large clients do not switch IT vendors lightly - the knowledge of their systems, the security clearances and the risk of a botched transition all favour the incumbent - and Infosys's ~21% margin (Screener EBITDA margin 23.7% in FY26 vs TCS 27.1%, HCLTech 20.6%, Wipro 19.2%) and 31.2% ROE show it. But the moat protects the relationship, not the price: clients can and do demand that AI productivity gains be passed on, and Infosys's own scale advantage - hundreds of thousands of engineers - matters less when software writes software. There is no product moat. If AI services do not grow fast enough, the moat will keep Infosys in the room while the bill gets smaller.

blocks.p: Infosys's revenue grew from ₹62,441 cr in FY16 to ₹1,78,650 cr in FY26, about 11% a year, and profit attributable to shareholders from ₹13,489 cr to ₹29,440 cr, about 8% a year. In dollars the story has two halves. FY21-23 was the post-Covid digital boom: US$ revenue rose from US$12.8 bn (FY20) to US$18.2 bn (FY23), 12.5% a year. Since then growth has been 1.9% (FY24), 3.9% (FY25) and 4.6% (FY26), about 3.4% a year, and in FY26 almost all of it came from price, not volume. A weaker rupee did much of the work in rupee terms: Infosys converted each dollar at ₹71 in FY20 and ₹88.6 in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Infosys is a mature, very profitable business that has stopped growing in real terms. sections.title: Almost all the cash goes back to shareholders: ₹1.3 lakh cr in six years

blocks.p: Infosys needs little capital: capex is ~1.5% of revenue and working capital grows slowly. Over FY21-26 it generated ₹1,64,466 cr of operating cash and spent ₹14,012 cr on capex. It returned ₹89,197 cr in dividends and ~₹41,000 cr through three buybacks (FY22, FY23 and the ₹18,000 cr tender at ₹1,800 in Dec-2025). The policy since FY25 is to return ~85% of free cash flow over five years through dividends and buybacks and to raise the dividend every year; FY25-26 returned 82.1%. Acquisitions are small and frequent (four in the last 18 months, the largest up to US$465 mn).

The question for the next five years is not how much cash comes back but what Infosys buys: management says it has "a good pipeline" of acquisitions in healthcare, telecom, financial services and AI-led service lines, and has decided not to invest in data centres. sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts, cash above profit, tax one-offs to strip out

bullets: **Cash backs profit.** Operating cash flow was 115% of attributable profit in FY26, 134% in FY25 and 96% in FY24; over FY15-26 cash from operations (₹2,39,440 cr) was 101% of profit. Free cash flow adjusted for the Labour Codes payments and tax refunds was 106% of profit in FY26 (company).

**Tax orders flatter some years.** Favourable orders under sections 250/254 of the Income Tax Act brought interest on refunds and reversals of old provisions: +₹4.76 of EPS in FY24 (₹1,933 cr of interest), +₹1.03 in FY25, and in FY26 ₹381 cr of interest plus ₹774 cr of tax reversals in Q4. We leave tax-refund interest out of our forecasts and show the forward P/E history both with and without these items.

**Other income is real but includes currency.** FY26 other income of ₹4,322 cr (AR note 2.19) was ₹2,693 cr of interest, ₹393 cr of gains on funds and bonds, ₹421 cr of tax-refund interest, a net ₹497 cr of exchange gains (₹2,451 cr of hedge losses against ₹2,948 cr of translation gains) and ₹318 cr of other items (incl. a ₹165 cr property gain). Screener nets the ₹1,289 cr Labour Codes charge into this row (₹3,033 cr).

**One-off charges are disclosed and small.** The Labour Codes charge (₹1,289 cr, Q3FY26) is a genuine one-off from new law; acquisition amortisation (~50 bp of margin in Q4FY26) is recurring as long as Infosys keeps buying companies.

**Revenue recognition.** Fixed-price contracts use percentage-of-completion estimates (the auditor's key audit matter); unbilled revenue is ~US$2 bn. Large deals are reported as total contract value over 3-5 years, not as revenue, and the conversion is slowing as renewals are repriced.

**Disclosure.** Good: eight verticals, four geographies, client buckets, utilisation, attrition, deal TCV and cash every quarter, in US$ and ₹. Weak: no disclosure of AI deflation, pricing or the revenue from GCC clients; "AI-first revenue" is the company's own definition.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit by Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP, cash conversion above 100%, no debt, and one-offs clearly flagged by the company. Watch acquisition accounting (earn-outs, retention pay) as M&A picks up, and the size of tax-order gains in the year they arrive.

blocks.p: Infosys has no financial debt; its only borrowings are ₹9,176 cr of lease liabilities (offices). By Jun-2026 it was ₹37,065 cr after the ₹25 final dividend (₹10,117 cr) and the Optimum and Stratus acquisitions. Trade receivables (₹35,234 cr) and unbilled revenue are the big operating assets; DSO fell to 63 days in Q1FY27, the lowest in years.

Turned round, on our ten-year forecasts the price of ₹994 implies long-run growth of about −2.4% a year: the market is pricing a business that shrinks after the next decade. That is the bear case; our target assumes the market applies the sector's de-rating to Infosys, not a deeper one.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a cash machine that has stopped growing, priced as one; BUY at 12.1x FY28E

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's second-largest IT services company, with ~2,000 large clients, a ~21% operating margin held for four years, free cash flow above profit, no debt, ~₹37,000 cr of cash and a policy of returning ~85% of free cash flow (a ~5.3% dividend yield on FY27E at ₹994, plus buybacks). AI services are 8.2% of revenue and growing fast.

**What you are paying:** 12.8x our FY27E and 12.1x FY28E EPS for a business whose organic growth is ~0.5% this year and ~3% in our later years, and whose core work is being repriced by AI. On the street's method and our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): BUY. Most of the upside is the multiple: we need the market to pay 16.5x Sep-28E EPS - the IT sector's median de-rating applied to Infosys's own history - against ~11.7x today. On the large incumbents' deeper de-rating alone the target would be ~₹1,190. On our cash flows the price already assumes long-run growth of about −2.4% a year.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Infosys (consolidated, Rs crore). Infosys is modelled in US dollars first: US$ revenue by vertical (the eight business segments the company discloses) in `usdBuild`, converted at a stated Rs/US$ path; the engine then runs on the resulting rupee revenue growth (`revenueGrowth`) and an EBITDA margin. EBITDA = Screener operating profit before other income and depreciation; the company's EBIT (operating) margin = EBITDA margin less depreciation & amortisation, which we show next to it. The authoring script checks that the US$ build times the Rs/US$ rate equals model revenue. Net profit is attributable to shareholders (tools/authoring/INFY.patch.js); the tax line also carries minorities. Other income = treasury yield on opening net cash + non-treasury items, built from the AR FY26 other-income note (2.19). Valued on P/E, as the street does.

usdBuild._why: US$ revenue by vertical. FY26 base = sum of the four quarters (US$ revenue x reported mix, fact sheets); total FY26 US$20,158 mn. FY27 guidance (23-Jul-2026): 1.5-3.0% constant currency, including ~1.7% from the Optimum Healthcare IT and Stratus acquisitions, >1% drag from a large European manufacturing client and 0.75-1% from moving work offshore; FS and EURS to grow above the company average, Retail and Communication weak. Q1FY27: +2.4% YoY cc, +1.0% QoQ (0.5% lost to an EURS programme termination). Growth rates are US$ (we assume no net cross-currency effect after Q1).

growthWhy.fs: FY27 +3.1%: grew 5.4% in FY26 and 2.8% (2.4% cc) in Q1FY27; ~US$1 bn of net new large-deal TCV in Q1 and Stratus (insurance, closed Apr-2026, ~0.25% of company revenue) inside it; management expects FS above the company average. FY28-29 +4.5%: large-deal ramp-ups, vendor consolidation, offset by AI-led price deflation on renewals.
growthWhy.mfg: FY27 -2%: lower revenue from one large European manufacturing client (>1% of company revenue; part of it a deal Infosys chose not to pursue, ending in December) and a weak European auto market; Q1 +1.5% YoY. FY28 +1% (the client is fully out of the base only from Q4FY27), FY29 +3%.
growthWhy.eurs: FY27 +2.5%: a client terminated a programme in Q1 (~0.5% of company revenue, one-off); management still expects EURS above average (80% of FY26 large-deal TCV was net new, utilities demand from grids and data centres). FY28-29 +4-4.5%.
growthWhy.retail: FY27 -1%: consumer budgets 'tightly controlled', clients asking for AI productivity commitments (Q1 -1.8% YoY). Slow recovery after.
growthWhy.comm: FY27 -0.5%: Q1 +2.9% YoY but management calls the vertical challenged and budgets flat to negative; FY26 growth came from large-deal ramp-ups that have now annualised. FY28 +2%, FY29 +2.5%.
growthWhy.hitech: FY27 flat: Q1 +1.6% YoY; tech clients are the earliest adopters of AI coding tools, which compresses classic work.
growthWhy.ls: FY27 +22%: Optimum Healthcare IT (agreement Mar-2026 for up to US$465 mn incl. earn-outs; closed in Q1FY27; ~1.5% of company revenue a year at a ~1.7% combined acquisition contribution less Stratus) plus ~2% organic. Q1FY27 life sciences +26.8% YoY. FY28 +6% (small carry-over), FY29 +5%.
growthWhy.others: Shrinking for two years (-12% YoY in Q1FY27); held flat after FY27.

fx._why: Rs/US$ conversion rate. FY26 average 88.6 (Rs178,650 cr / US$20,158 mn); Q1FY27 94.9 (Rs48,211 cr / US$5,082 mn); spot 95.81 at the 30-Sep-2026 close (PTI). FY27 95.5 = Q1 actual, ~95.6 for Q2 and the 30-Sep spot for H2. FY28-29: ~2% depreciation a year, roughly the rupee's forward premium and well below its ~3.7% a year average fall since FY20 on Infosys's own conversion rates (71.0 in FY20). Each 1% of rupee depreciation adds 15-17 bp to the operating margin (CFO, Jul-2026), before any reinvestment.

assumptions._revenueWhy: Rupee revenue = US$ build x Rs/US$. US$ growth +2.0% (FY27E), +3.0% (FY28E), +3.6% (FY29E); rupee growth +9.9% / +5.2% / +5.7%, of which ~7.8 / 2.1 / 2.1 points are the weaker rupee. FY27: Q1 US$5,082 mn; we assume Q2 +1.5% QoQ (full quarter of Optimum), Q3-Q4 roughly flat (furloughs, the European client's deal ending in December), i.e. ~2% cc, close to the 2.25% guidance midpoint and PL's 2.0%. FY28-29: organic growth of 3-3.5% - AI services (8.2% of revenue in Q1FY27, growing double digits a quarter) and large-deal ramp-ups offset 3-3.5% a year of AI-led price deflation on the rest (Kotak's assumption, Jul-2026). No acquisitions after Optimum/Stratus are assumed; Versent (75% for up to A$233 mn, pending regulatory approval) is excluded, as in the company's guidance.
assumptions._marginWhy: Company EBIT (operating) margin: 21.1% (FY25), 21.0% adjusted / 20.3% reported (FY26, Labour Codes charge Rs1,289 cr), 21.1% in Q1FY27; guidance 20-22% kept in Jul-2026. We model EBIT of ~21.0% in each year: rupee depreciation (+70 bp in Q1 alone) and Project Maximus (pricing, utilisation 84.9%, offshore mix, lean automation: +20-30 bp a quarter) offset wage hikes (October 2026 for most staff, January 2027 for seniors), ~50 bp of acquisition costs (amortisation, retention pay) and AI investments; FY28-29 carry AI price deflation against continued offshoring. EBITDA margin (Screener basis) = EBIT + D&A (~2.6% of revenue): FY26 23.7%, Q1FY27 23.7%. Brokers (Jul-2026) model EBIT of 19.8-21.3% for FY27-28.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs2,201 cr (FY24), Rs2,237 cr (FY25), Rs2,727 cr (FY26) = ~1.5% of revenue; we assume Rs2,900 / 3,000 / 3,200 cr. FY27E also includes ~Rs4,400 cr for the Optimum Healthcare IT and Stratus acquisitions (goodwill and intangibles rose US$466 mn in Q1FY27, IFRS balance sheet): an engine workaround, because the model has no acquisition line. Putting the purchase price into FY27 capex takes the cash out of the treasury and lets the acquired intangibles amortise through depreciation. The DCF starts in FY28 and is unaffected.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs4,902 cr = 8.6% of average gross block (Rs57,227 cr; Screener's gross block includes goodwill and right-of-use assets). Q1FY27 Rs1,246 cr (Rs4,984 cr annualised) before a full quarter of the new acquisitions. 8.0% on a gross block lifted by the FY27 acquisitions gives ~Rs5,100 cr in FY27E (2.6% of revenue), ~Rs5,500 cr in FY28E.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to OPENING net cash on Screener's basis (cash Rs22,201 cr + investments Rs21,880 cr - lease liabilities Rs9,176 cr = Rs34,905 cr at Mar-26). The company earned 6.7% on its gross cash and investments in FY26 and 6.8% in Q1FY27 (CFO). 9.0% on opening net cash equals ~6.6-6.9% on the average gross balance in our forecasts, because lease interest is charged separately (interest line) and cash builds through the year; the report shows the implied gross yield for each year. FY26 treasury income (AR note 2.19): interest Rs2,693 cr + gains on funds and bonds Rs393 cr = Rs3,086 cr on average cash and investments of Rs45,312 cr (6.8%).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income, only recurring items (AR FY26 note 2.19): net exchange gains (forward/option losses Rs2,451 cr against translation gains Rs2,948 cr = +Rs497 cr; FY25 +Rs259 cr) and miscellaneous income excluding the Rs165 cr profit on sale of property (Rs153 cr). We hold Rs650 cr. Left out as non-recurring: interest on income-tax refunds (Rs421 cr FY26, Rs343 cr FY25, Rs1,933 cr FY24) and property sale gains. FY27E total other income ~Rs3,790 cr vs Rs3,736 cr underlying in FY26 (Rs4,322 cr less tax-refund interest and the property gain) and Rs3,883 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (Screener Rs2,975 cr plus the Labour Codes charge, less Q4FY26 tax-refund interest): flat, because the Rs18,000 cr buyback (Dec-2025) cut the cash pile by about a third before it rebuilds.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs416 cr; Q1FY27 Rs119 cr (more leases with the acquisitions). No borrowings other than leases (Rs9,176 cr at Mar-26).
assumptions._taxWhy: Guidance: effective tax rate 29-30% for FY27 (Apr and Jul 2026). Q1FY27 29.5% (Rs3,253 cr on Rs11,028 cr). FY26 26.3% reported, flattered by Rs774 cr of reversals of prior-year provisions after favourable tax orders. 29.6% includes minorities (~0.1% of PBT; Rs34 cr in FY26). SEZ tax holidays keep expiring, so we do not assume a lower rate later.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividends only. FY26 DPS Rs48 (interim Rs23 + final Rs25) = 67% of reported EPS of Rs71.58; FY25 Rs43 (67%). Policy (from FY25): return ~85% of free cash flow over five years through dividends and/or buybacks/special dividends and raise the DPS every year; FY25-26 returned Rs55,523 cr = 82.1% of FCF incl. the Rs18,000 cr buyback. The engine cannot reduce the share count, so the buyback part of the policy (~20% of profit a year) stays in the treasury and earns interest; at a P/E of ~12x a buyback would add ~1% more to EPS a year than the interest, which we leave out (conservative).

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, cash-rich, but now exposed to a technology shift that could shrink its core market; 0.9 gives an 11.9% cost of equity, above the 11.3% we use for defensive consumer franchises.
dcf._tgWhy: Rupee terminal growth of 5%: ~3% US$ growth for a mature services company plus ~2% rupee depreciation. Below the 5-6% house range for domestic compounders because AI may shrink the traditional services pool.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Rupee revenue growth fades from ~5.6% (FY29E) to 5.5% over ten years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades from 23.7% to 23.0% (EBIT ~20.4%, the bottom half of today's 20-22% band): AI deflation and pricing pressure erode margins slowly.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~1.5% of revenue, as in FY24-26.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Infosys: P/E on FY28E EPS (Motilal Oswal and 360 ONE 14x, PL and Choice 15x, ICICI Securities, Nirmal Bang and Nuvama 13x; Jul-2026). 16.5x = Infosys's 23.3x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (forwardMedian; no trough years; 23.8x on EPS before tax-order one-offs) cut by the -29.0% median de-rating of the IT peer set versus each peer's five-year median P/E at the 30-Sep-2026 close (TCS -53%, Wipro -40%, LTIMindtree -38%, LTTS -31%, Mphasis -27%, HCLTech -21%, Persistent -18%, Coforge -11%) = 16.55x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. House rule for all IT reports: full peer set, excluding the company itself and Tech Mahindra (its FY24-25 earnings trough distorts both its current and its median P/E); no sub-sets. No growth or returns adjustment. Sensitivity: on the three large incumbents only (TCS, Wipro, HCLTech; median -40%) the multiple would be 14x. Cross-checks: a justified P/E of 13.7x (90% cash payout, 11.9% cost of equity, 5% growth); 16.5x needs ~6.1% long-run growth. Bull 20x (its 25th-percentile forward P/E since 2021, 19.7x); bear 11x (justified P/E at 4% growth, ~15% below its lowest forward P/E since 2021).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 10x Sep-28E EBITDA = Infosys's 16.6x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, cut by the same -29% IT sector de-rating (11.8x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~15% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (Rs43,745 cr) = 10.2x, rounded. Bull 12x, bear 7x scale with the P/E multiples.
